A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
S. halstedii JM 8 produces an endoglucanse and a cellulose binding protein that are co-transcribed and regulated by a TTA in the first gene.

S. halstedii JM 8 produces a novel type of cellulase that is first produced in the form of an inactive precursor (p42) that is later processed to the active form (Cel2) and that this precursor is co-transcribed with an ORF that encodes a protein (p40) with high affinity for crystalline cellulose.
the p40 protein, although it does not have any detectable activity, is essential for the processing of the p42 precursor into its mature form and for the production of Cel2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a gene encoding a cellulose-binding domain is clustered with a gene encoding an endoglulcanase.
the two genes are co-regulated by the bldA gene product, and the p42 and p40 proteins are processed in old cultures.
